rows.note: This is the all-purpose possessive form for saying something belongs to him without a following noun.

example.jyutping: nei1 bun2 syu1 hai6 keoi5 ge3

rows.note: This is the all-purpose possessive used before a noun to mean belonging to him.

example.jyutping: ngo5 wan2 dou2 keoi5 ge3 ngan4 baau1 laa3

rows.note: Use this colloquial pattern when the noun naturally takes a classifier, such as 佢個袋 for “his bag.”

example.english: His bag is on the floor.
example.jyutping: keoi5 go3 doi6 hai2 dei6 haa6

rows.note: Use this when “his place” specifically means his home or household.

example.english: I’m going to his home for dinner tonight.
example.jyutping: ngo5 gam1 maan5 heoi3 keoi5 uk1 kei2 sik6 faan6

rows.note: Use this casual form for his place as a destination or location, especially when the exact type of place is unimportant.

example.english: Let’s go to his place together after work.
example.traditional: 放工之後一齊去佢度啦。
example.jyutping: fong3 gung1 zi1 hau6 jat1 cai4 heoi3 keoi5 dou6 laa1
